verdicts.title: Foundational theory for optimal decision tree problems. I. Algorithmic and geometric foundations
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
In the first paper (part I) of this series of two, we introduce four novel definitions of the ODT problems: three for size-constrained trees and one for depth-constrained trees. These definitions are stated unambiguously through executable recursive programs, satisfying all criteria we propose for a formal specification. In this sense, they resemble the "standard form" used in the study of general-purpose solvers.

verdicts.title: Solomon's induction in quasi-elementary groups
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Given a finite group G, we address the following question: which multiples of the trivial representation are linear combinations of inductions of trivial representations from proper subgroups of G? By Solomon's induction theorem, all multiples are if G is not quasi-elementary. We complement this by showing that all multiples of p are if G is p-quasi-elementary and not cyclic, and that this is best possible.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns Solomon's induction theorem for representations of quasi-elementary groups, which has no bearing on quandles, syntactic monoids of Boolean formulas, or DPLL search tree height.
